fields.sample_size: 12 semi-structured virtual interviews (45-60 minutes) with government, nonprofit and utility providers of WASH services for unsheltered people in five West Coast areas (Los Angeles, Portland, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle; all among the 15 US Continuums of Care with the most unsheltered people in 2022): 29 providers were invited after a desk review, further contacts came by snowball, and a validation workshop was held with participants; interviews were audio-recorded with oral consent and professionally transcribed; the authors argue theme saturation with this small sample
fields.effect_measure: qualitative themes (motivation, operations, funding, key partners, measuring impact); no quantitative estimate
fields.effect_estimate: Providers described four intervention types (porta-potties, public water access points, hygiene stations, mobile showers). Most cited WASH as a human right as a motivation, alongside public health (COVID-19, hepatitis A and shigella outbreaks) and dignity; programmes were ad hoc, run by local champions in nonprofits, local government and utilities, and struggled to secure long-term funding. Participants said no government department had clear responsibility and that an advocate inside government was needed to navigate permits; impact data were basic (guests served, hygiene kits distributed, water volume at public taps). The sample is small and results are reported by theme rather than by city.
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: CASP Qualitative per-item (re-appraised 2026-10-09 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating): 1(aims)=Yes; 2(qual approach)=Yes; 3(design)=Yes (exploratory design; five sites chosen from the 15 Continuums of Care with most unsheltered people); 4(recruitment)=Yes (29 providers invited from a desk review, 12 interviewed, snowball referrals; the small sample is acknowledged); 5(data collection)=Yes (semi-structured interviews with a guide in the supplement, recorded and professionally transcribed, plus a validation workshop); 6(researcher-participant)=Can't tell (not discussed); 7(ethics)=Yes (oral informed consent, de-identified, University of Pennsylvania exempt protocol 851928); 8(analysis rigor)=Can't tell (iterative inductive coding with a code dictionary in the supplement and participant validation, but the number of coders and the handling of contradictory data are not reported); 9(findings)=Yes; 10(value)=Yes. Per CASP's own guidance no composite score is computed.

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative interview study of WASH services for unsheltered people in five West Coast US areas (12 interviews with providers, plus a validation workshop); no estimate of access outcomes; read in full text 2026-10-09.
